turns.summary: Brynjar rested at the waygate stone and woke at dawn to find a dead sheep on the track — the first sign the Riven Marches livestock sickness has reached this road.
turns.narration:
You find a hollow in the lee of the waygate stone — the iron ring above you catching the last of the night wind — and spread your bedroll on ground that is cold but dry enough. Freki circles twice and drops against your side, a warm press of wire coat and slow breath. Sleep comes without argument.

Dawn arrives gray and honest. The melt has softened the track overnight; boot-prints from yesterday are deeper now, edges blurred by the slow seep. The waygate stone stands as it did — the broken top, the iron ring hammered in crooked — but the light is different, the shadow thrown spinward across the path rather than widdershins. Your body feels the night's work undone. Freki is already on her feet, nose moving along the ground in widening arcs, reading the night's traffic.

Something she finds makes her pause — not a growl, not alarm, but the focused stillness she gets when something is worth your attention. A few yards along the track toward the Marchward, there is a dead sheep. Not torn, not dragged. It simply lay down in the night and did not get up, and whoever owns it has not yet come looking. The fleece is patchy in a way you have seen before on animals that stopped eating weeks before they died. You think of the news that has been drifting up the road — the Riven Marches herds, the quiet sickness spreading flock to flock — and the dead animal at a waygate feels less like bad luck and more like a marker.

turns.player: I wanted to head to the waygate in the crossing
turns.summary: Brynjar walked the hubward road from the waygate stone to The Crossing, arriving at the waygate arch by early afternoon.
turns.narration:
The Waygate stone is already behind you before the morning is properly up — Freki ranging ahead on the softened track, nose working the cold air in long sweeps. The dead sheep stays where it lay. You leave it for whatever the valley sends to deal with it.

The road runs hubward through young spring mud and the last grey stands of elder-scrub, the melt still working its way out of the ditches. By midday the ground firms a little and the track widens where other feet have worn it smooth over years of the same crossing. Freki drops back to your heel as the waygate traffic thickens — a carter moving spinward with a load of lime, two women in Lattice-Cities grey walking without speaking, a Marcher leaning on a post at a junction who looks at you once, top to bottom, and says: "Your left side opens when you're tired. Sleep on it." Then he looks away. Not a threat. A reading. He is already watching the road again before you can decide whether to answer.

The Crossing's waygate is a different thing from the broken stone north of the Marchward — a proper threshold, the arch dressed with flat iron fittings, the ground worn to smooth stone within ten paces of it by decades of feet. It is early afternoon when you walk under it, Freki close, the shadow of the iron ring falling across your shoulder. The Crossing Hub Hall is visible through the arch — the octagonal walls, the chalk-board column at the center, the eight thresholds each facing a different spoke of the valley.

turns.player: Hang back at the arch and watch who comes and goes — see if anything moves through here that matches what you know of Stillhold operatives or Kjotve's kind of people
turns.summary: Brynjar watched the Crossing waygate at dusk — nothing obvious, but a heavy-wool man who read the ironwork before the faces passed through heading hubward, and Freki logged him.
turns.narration:
You pull back from the arch proper and find a spot against the worn stone of the gatehouse wall — close enough to read faces, far enough that you're just another traveler resting a leg. Freki settles at your foot without being told, wire coat flat, yellow-green eyes tracking the same stream of people yours do. She's already doing the work.

The evening traffic through the Crossing waygate is steady but thin — a pair of lime-traders heading widdershins, a woman in the long grey of a Lattice-Cities inspector who walks through without stopping, two farmhands with a mule loaded past sensible, a young man in road-worn boots who pays his chalk-mark at the column and vanishes spinward. None of it rings wrong. You're reading for two kinds: Stillhold-quiet people who don't check in, who carry cords and move without luggage, and Kjotve's sort — fighters who hold themselves like the world owes them room. You see neither. What you do see is the pattern beneath the pattern — who checks the column before they look at faces, who checks faces first. The Lattice-Cities inspector checked the column. Everyone else checked faces. One man, heavy wool, a drover's gait but no animals, checked the arch itself — the ironwork specifically — before he checked anything. He came from the spinward road, walked through without stopping, and was hubward before you'd placed him fully. Not wrong, exactly. But the wrong kind of careful.

Freki's ears go flat for two beats and then settle. Not a growl — the thing between a growl and a held breath. You glance down. She's already watching the arch again, but her weight has shifted forward a fraction, the way it does when something registered and she's decided it's gone.

*You feel it settle into you — a new steadiness. (Level 2: +1 attunement, +5 reserves, and growth to choose — a sub-attribute point and a skill point.)*

turns.player: Follow the heavy-wool man hubward — Freki flagged him, and a loose tail costs nothing yet
turns.summary: Brynjar tailed the heavy-wool man through the Hub Hall but lost him in the dark of a spinward road — the man moved too fast and too certain, and the night took the gap.
turns.narration:
You push off the gatehouse wall and drift hubward after him — not rushing, just a traveler heading the same direction. Freki falls in at your left knee without a word from you, her gait loose and unhurried, nose down.

The Hub Hall swallows you both. The octagonal space is lit by four iron lanterns and smells of chalk dust and wet wool. Eight threshold arches open off it like spokes, and the chalk-board column at the center draws a cluster of three people comparing marks. The heavy-wool man moves through all of it without slowing — no hesitation, no check of the column, no pause at any arch. He knows exactly which spoke he wants. By the time you've read the room and picked him out of the lantern-shadow, he's already committed to one of the far arches and through it, the threshold swallowing him whole.

You reach the arch he took a breath later. A spinward road stretches out into the dark, the mud catching the last bleed of lantern-light for maybe twenty paces before it dissolves into nothing. He could be anywhere in that. Freki stands at the threshold, one paw over the line, and holds — she won't push into the dark on a cold trail she's not sure of, and you read the set of her ears as clearly as speech. She marked him. She'll know him again. But tonight the dark won the gap.

You stand at the arch a moment longer, memorizing what you can: spinward road, deliberate stride, a man who checked the ironwork before the faces. Whatever he was confirming, the waygate itself was the thing he needed to verify — and he verified it and left.

turns.player: Let him go for tonight — find a place to sleep inside the Crossing and pick this up in the morning with a fresh eye
turns.summary: Brynjar let the heavy-wool man go into the dark and took a room in the waygate wardroom, sleeping the night with Freki against his legs.
turns.narration:
You let the dark have him. A tail through an unfamiliar waygate in full night, against a man who already knows his route — that is not a tail, that is a gift. You pull Freki back from the spinward threshold with a low word and she comes, though she holds at the arch a beat longer than you, nose lifted, logging the last thread of his scent before she turns.

The Hub Hall settles around you. The three travelers at the chalk column have found their marks and drifted through their respective arches, and the space is quieter now — just the four lanterns and the sound of wind finding the threshold gaps. The stone underfoot is worn to a smooth basin at the center from decades of the same feet turning the same way. You read the arches and pick the one that looks most like it leads to something with a roof and a fire.

A waygate wardroom opens off the hall's northeast face — a narrow door, hardly marked, but the kind of door that has always been there. The warden inside is a spare man in his fifties with a tally-stick and no interest in your business beyond the usual questions: where from, where bound, any animals. You say the road south, you say hubward come morning, you say yes, one dog. He marks his stick and points at a low-ceilinged dormer up a short stair — straw pallets, two other travelers already asleep, and a clay lamp burning low on a shelf. Freki circles once and drops against your legs the moment you sit, and that is enough warmth.

You sleep. Whatever the heavy-wool man is carrying hubward, it will still be moving come morning — and you will be rested when you think about what it means that he read the ironwork before he read the faces.

form: Stocky, average-height man with pale skin and icy blue eyes. Chestnut hair shaved at sides and back, long on top and knotted. Thick beard with two braids flanking the mouth. A dark blue Norse dragon-knot tattoo curls from behind his ear to his temple; vertical dark blue rune tattoos descend from above his brows, over both eyes and cheeks, into the beard. Blue tunic with light red cuff-and-collar accents, dark grey puffy trousers, dark blue shin-wraps over leather boots. Silver arm ring with two dragon heads on the right arm. Bronze-inlaid one-handed axe at the hip, seax at the back of the belt, pouches at the front.

bio.hometown: A northern village called Javiksholm but it was raided and razed.
bio.residence: They’ve been on the road joined by their hound Freki
bio.livelihood: Hunting and trading on the road
bio.motivation: They were forced to flee from the raid that killed their father and razed their home village.
bio.story: Brynjar had fled from his village of Javiksholm during the raid as his father commanded. On his way out of the longhouse he made sure to grab his axe and shield. He also was followed by his dog Freki. Before he had fully escaped the village he looked back towards the longhouse and saw his father Andyr fighting off many of the raiders until one, the leader of this raid and a rival Jarl Kjotve Olafsson, who wanted the land Brynjar’s clan had owned due to its fertile fields and prime oceanfront access. Kjotve had locked into a duel with Andyr until he started loosing and he had one of his men strike him in the back with a spear, then it was all over. Kjotve had ordered his men to toss his body into the ocean and burn the longhouse down. After seeing this Brynjar had fled and escaped from the village. He has been on the road ever since surviving off of hunting wild game and trading with villages and traders he passed along the way, which leads us here.

[d1] Three bills posted: a filled labor posting for road-clearing east toward the Stillhold; a waygate truce-law notice requiring all arrivals to present at the Wardhouse within the hour with arms checked; and a missing-person posting for Sera of the Stillhold — grey cloak, dark braid, last seen at the…
[d?] you have walked here
[d1] All arrivals must present at the Wardhouse within the hour by truce-law; arms are checked on the rack inside. The duty officer logs names, origins, and any declaration of blood business.

[d1] The Wardhouse posts a weekly night-watch vacancy for travelers without permanent standing — meal, floor space, and a half-copper per watch. Road-clearing east toward the Stillhold is already taken.
[d1] The nearest way gate is half a morning north of the Marchward Wardhouse, marked by a broken stone with an iron ring hammered into it — on the waystone track heading hubward from the town.

[d2] Livestock Sickness of the Riven Marches — A dead sheep found at the waygate road at dawn — fleece patchy, no signs of predation, died lying down. The pattern matches what has been said of the Riven Marches herds: animals that stopped eating weeks before they collapsed. The sickness may be moving…
[d2] The Crossing waygate wardroom offers overnight stays for travelers — narrow door off the Hub Hall's northeast face, tally-stick intake, straw dormer above.

kjotve-olafsson.label: Kjotve Olafsson
facts: [d1] Jarl who led the raid on Javiksholm. Won Andyr's land by having a spearman strike Andyr from behind mid-duel — a formal fight turned to murder when Kjotve was losing. Now holds Javiksholm's fields and shore. Andyr's body was thrown into the ocean.
[d1] met in play

[d1] Ragnar Solmyr recognized Kjotve's name and reputation without prompting — called it 'not the kind that travels well.' Under Marcher custom, a back-strike in a sworn duel is disqualifying; a man shouldn't be able to hold land taken that way. Ragnar also noted Kjotve doesn't travel alone.

facts: [d1] Brynjar's home village — raided and razed by Kjotve Olafsson. Andyr died here, struck from behind. The longhouse was burned. Kjotve now holds the fertile fields and the oceanfront.

brynjar-andyrsson-thread.label: The Oath on Kjotve
facts: [d1] Brynjar swore aloud, to his father and the gods, to kill Kjotve Olafsson — but to do it with more honor than Kjotve ever showed. The oath is spoken and cannot be unsaid.

sera-of-the-stillhold.label: Sera of the Stillhold
facts: [d1] Freki read the cloth bundle — dried white-flowered sprig and knotted cord — and tracked toward the side door Sera used before dawn. The trail leads east, to a fork: waygate approach north, Stillhold road south.

[d1] Freki confirmed the trail at the fork goes south — toward the Stillhold road. Ragnar saw two people at the south fork before full light. Sera was not alone when she left, or someone followed her.

[d1] Two sets of prints at the south fork: a lighter frame went first, a heavier follower came ten minutes behind. Sera was not alone — someone tracked her, or met her, on the Stillhold road. Time of passage: roughly three to four hours before the Marchward woke.

[d1] Freki confirmed the lighter prints as Sera's — she was moving fast, not walking. Ragnar reads it as someone who knows where they're going or doesn't want to be seen; the gait is the same either way.

[d1] The heavier follower's prints read as deliberate pursuit — weight forward, toe-heavy, pace quickening as sight-lines opened south. Not a soldier, not a hunter. Someone closing distance on a target they knew was ahead.
[d1] The shimmer pressed into the heavier follower's heel-strike vanished on direct examination — gone before it could be named, leaving no second trace and no pattern in the surrounding mud.

[d1] At the waypost junction half a mile south of the Marchward east fork, Sera's trail continued south unchanged while her heavier follower turned east into an ash copse — a watching position with a clear line to the junction road. The follower stopped pursuing and began observing.

[d1] At the waypost junction, the follower stopped, watched Sera walk south until she was out of sight, then withdrew deliberately into the ash copse and left — not spooked, not chased. A planned observation with a clean exit. The copse is empty now.

A second person sat at the bar that night, left a folded linen containing a dried white-flowered sprig and knotted cord, and departed before dawn. Tracking confirms Sera moved fast south on the Stillhold road while a heavier follower pursued her with deliberate intent—until the follower stopped at a waypost junction, observed Sera until she passed out of sight, then withdrew into an ash copse and left without being chased. [d1] Arrived alone seven days ago — unusual; checked in properly, no declared business, asked for lodging at the Crow and Thistle. Room empty next morning, innkeep Doss didn't see her leave. Family posted the bill knowing roughly why she came but wanting her back without questions.

[d1] A second person was present the evening Sera stayed — sat at the third stool, watched her without speaking, left before dawn, left behind a folded linen with a dried white-flowered sprig and a knotted cord. The cord-knot's meaning is unknown. Freki reads the stool as a live trail.
